title: modular monolith layered hexagonal clean architecture
concepts: Architecture styles organize the dependencies, boundaries, and runtime shape of a system; names such as layered, hexagonal, and clean describe overlapping ways to structure boundaries rather than mutually exclusive deployment products.

A modular monolith runs as one deployable application while enforcing internal module boundaries; it can preserve simpler deployment and transactions while allowing teams to defer distributed-system costs.
Layered architecture separates responsibilities such as presentation, application, domain, and infrastructure, but teams must decide which dependency directions and cross-layer calls are permitted.
Hexagonal architecture models an application core surrounded by ports and adapters; the geometric name does not prescribe six layers or six interfaces.
Clean Architecture places policy at the center and directs source dependencies inward; compile-time references and runtime calls can point differently, so diagrams must distinguish them.
Boundaries create translation and indirection costs. Use them where independent change, testing, or replacement matters, and avoid empty layers and interfaces that add no meaningful seam.
